entries: Dr. Viktra Mordenheim's greatest invention is also her worst mistake: Adam, an automaton imprinted with the neuroprint of Viktra's dead lover. Adam's hulking figure and disheveled appearance are a result of his final struggle with Viktra, which also resulted in Adam's memories being corrupted. He now haunts the halls of Mordenheim Kinetics, searching for clues that might explain his monstrous nature and why the doctor hunts him.
Adam is described in more detail in the "{@book Personnel Directory|PL|3|Adam}" section.
The founder and president of Mordenheim Kinetics is an eccentric visionary, unparalleled technologist, and notorious recluse.

The stat block in this section is based on the Viktra Mordenheim stat block in{@i Ravenloft: The Horrors Within}. You can use the additional details and rules in that book to further describe Viktra and emphasize her ability to control her domain.
Viktra is described in more detail in the "{@book Personnel Directory|PL|3|Viktra Mordenheim}" section.
The created are Chief Engineer Hendrik von Aubrecker's attempt to replicate and improve upon Dr. Mordenheim's incredible humanlike automaton, Adam.

At his project's outset, Hendrik crafted a custom neuroprint by combining his own neuroprint with neuroprints from each of his siblings. Hendrik injects all of his created with the same copy of this chimeric neuroprint, but no two created are the same. Each created manifests a unique combination of the three von Aubreckers' intellects, obsessions, and personality flaws. The only things the created have in common are their violent dispositions toward anyone but the von Aubreckers and their tendency to go haywire when physically damaged.

Though his ultimate goal is to perfectly replicate the human form, Hendrik is no artist, and he lacks access to realistic fabricated flesh and textiles. He clumsily enrobes his creations with what materials he has on hand—contrivances that only emphasize the created's artificial nature. Roll on or choose a result from the Created Facade table to inspire the eerie appearance of a created.

rows: Clothes patched together from discarded lab coats, protective goggles, and disposable gloves.
Hair made from tangles of copper wiring and plastic tubing.
Nonfunctional extra limbs stolen from other created.
Digits and extremities cobbled together from ordinary office stationery.
Jewelry made from microscope lenses, circuit wires, and electrical diodes.

entries: Once an empty echo is injected with a neuroprint, it becomes a fully functional echo. Beneath its sturdy mechanical frame, an echo has all the same memories and personality traits as its neuroprint donor, also called the echo's agent.

As an echo, an agent retains all of its learned skills and talents but none of its muscle memory. It can take months or even years before an agent is able to perform once-routine activities in its new echo body. Most echoes succumb to Spontaneous Echo Malfunction before regaining their full motoric functions.

An echo is "empty" until imprinted with its agent's neuroprint. While empty, an echo possesses just enough computing power to move around and perform basic tasks on its own, though it lacks the ability to reason, feel emotions, or form memories.

Unsupervised, empty echoes have the unsettling tendency to self-activate, leave their storage units, and wander the halls of Mordenheim Kinetics. Even more unsettlingly, an empty echo's only means of verbal communication is to emit an ear-piercing screech. Technicians are advised to wear hearing protection at all times when working on empty echoes.

Towering, fierce Gerta may be the youngest von Aubrecker, but she looms over her brothers in both stature and force of personality. Gerta's custom plasteel skeleton and weatherproofed chassis protect her from the dangers of her work with dormant empty echoes in the Cryogenics department.

Hendrik has modified his body to truly monstrous effect. In place of bones and organs, Hendrik has a carbon fiber exoskeleton and a self-recharging engine in his rib cage. Hydraulic pistons give Hendrik incredible speed and enable him to deliver devastating blows. For particularly elusive enemies, Hendrik employs syringes full of potent sedatives from his third arm.
Shaped like a hunting dog and programmed to be five times as vicious, the Mordenheim Kinetics K-Nine unit is a combat machine designed for tactical warfare and conflict suppression.

When funding for Mordenheim Kinetics' primary ventures started to dwindle, Dr. Mordenheim turned to less scrupulous clients for capital. The K-Nine is one of the company's most successful creations developed for military defense contractors and private mercenary groups.

Before Mordenheim Kinetics' fall into ruin, K-Nine prototypes and deactivated units decorated the facility's lobbies. Now, packs of the mechanical hounds stalk the campus like feral wolves, hunting down and forcibly disabling escaped experiments and wayward visitors alike.

Despite his near-total transformation into a technological monster, Rudolph remains the most charming of the von Aubrecker siblings. All that remain of the elder brother's original form are his handsome face and formidable brain; the latter is augmented by cybernetic enhancements that amplify his mental powers to supernatural levels.

A shattered echo is an echo that has undergone Spontaneous Echo Malfunction (SEM). Both empty echoes and neuroprint-injected echoes are susceptible to the phenomenon, which has no known cause. Signs of a shattered echo include unpredictable movements, murderous outbursts, and violent hallucinations. Once an echo has shattered, it's impossible to repair the echo's neuroprint or return the echo to working condition.

If a shattered echo had an agent before undergoing SEM, it often retains corrupted fragments of its agent's memories and personality. Such shattered echoes might attempt to reenact disjointed memories or chirp half-remembered bits of overheard dialogue. Though such behaviors may give the impression of a latent intellect, they're in fact nothing more than misfiring bits of computer code.
